processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea, described as adaptable in what it can be made into. The processing follows whichever tea its leaf goes into.
harvest_season: A mid-season cultivar; picking is done in timely batches, and as with other Chinese greens the spring shoots are most valued.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it; the fresh shoots are plump and yellow-green with few hairs.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the tea made; as a green tea, typically a light yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Lanceolate green leaves of medium size with a clearly raised surface, typically soft when steeped as a green tea.
taste_profile: No tasting record specific to this cultivar is well established. Spring shoots test at about 27.4% polyphenols and about 2.7 to 3% amino acids, a moderate balance.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Chinese green tea made from it; follow the tea's own style if it was made otherwise.

vintage_note: Seldom sold under its own name. Its leaf goes into regional teas, which are sold according to their class; green teas are usually the current spring harvest.
description:
Zhuyeqi No. 12 is a tea plant, not a tea you order by name. It is a clonal cultivar from the Tea Research Institute of the Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, a medium-leaf bush valued in the field for yield and hardiness.

The bush has a half-open habit and fairly sparse branches, with lance-shaped, raised green leaves. Its shoots are plump and yellow-green with little hair and stay tender for a good while, and at six years old a garden can reach 262 kg per 667 square metres.

In the cup there is no well-established profile of its own, because it depends on the tea being made. Its chemistry is moderate, so a careful maker has room to work; brew whatever you get according to its style.

It grows mainly in Hunan and has been planted widely in Henan, Jiangxi and Anhui. For a drinker it is mostly a useful detail on a label, a clue that the leaf comes from a modern bred plant.
history: Bred by the Tea Research Institute of the Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences. Its registration appears under two numbers, Huacha 68 (GSCT 68) and GS13016-1994, and little is documented beyond that about its release.
